newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower on profit taking.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly lower, pulled down by light profit-taking after Wednesday's strong runup.

September Treasury bond futures extended the uptrend early in the session, reaching as high as 115-02, then spent the rest of the day consolidating midrange before slumping to a fresh low shortly before the close.
Options-related activity tied to Friday's expiration of August contracts contributed to early gains, floor traders said.
One trading firm sold about 6,000 of the August 115-00 Treasury bond calls, prompting short-covering in the September bond futures contract, floor traders said.
Bond futures were also underpinned as a buy-the-dips attitude buttressed the contract on pullbacks, traders said.
"Every dip in the market has been bought aggressively by some of the medium- and longer-term players," a broker said.
He called the day's price action neutral from a technical perspective.
"People are just waiting for either stronger data to get short or for a setback to create a buying opportunity," the broker added.

This morning's stronger than expected Philadelphia Federal Reserve Bank business survey weighed on Treasurys. The bank's July index rose to 28.1 from 25.2 in June. Traders had anticipated a pullback to 18.
An earlier round of economic data had little price impact. Inital weekly jobless claims fell to 349,000 from 377,000 a week earlier. The forecast had been for a 345,000 reading.
June housing starts rose 4.8 percent to a 1.452 million annualized rate, in line with market expectations.
September T-bonds ended 1/32 lower at 114-21/32, 10-year notes were unchanged at 109-26/32, and December Eurodollars unchanged at 94.065. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
